description: Volume, outcome, failure location and latency for schema registry operations (check, publish, delete, version promotion, schema push), each in its own row, plus the health of the dependencies they call: schema-service composition, policy-service, ClickHouse usage lookups for conditional breaking changes, CDN artifact writes, schema-change webhook jobs and the per-target registry lock. Rejected is an expected outcome (composition errors, breaking changes, policy violations, contract failures, invalid input); only unexpected errors indicate a Hive-side problem.

panels.description: Completed schema registry operations in the selected range by action. Every operation that returned a result or threw is counted, whatever its outcome.
panels.title: Operations by action

panels.description: Percentage of completed check, publish, delete, promotion and push operations that ended in an unexpected (non-HiveError) error. Rejected results and expected domain errors such as invalid input or authorization failures count as successfully handled.
panels.title: Unexpected error rate

panels.description: Completed operations per chart interval by action. Log scale so low-volume actions stay visible.
panels.title: Operations over time by action

panels.description: Unexpected failures per chart interval grouped by action and error source. Expected domain errors are not failures. Postgres errors currently carry no source and appear as 'unknown'.
panels.title: Unexpected errors over time by action and source

panels.description: Share of unexpected errors across check, publish, delete, promotion and push by the subsystem that raised them (schema-service, schema-policy-service, clickhouse, github, s3, commerce-service). Postgres errors currently carry no source and appear as 'unknown'.
panels.title: Unexpected errors by source

panels.description: Schema checks completed in the selected range. Rejected bundles composition errors, breaking changes, policy violations, contract failures and invalid input (including GitHub integration input); accepted includes checks skipped because nothing changed versus the latest composable version. Unexpected error counts checks that threw a non-HiveError and were therefore never counted as accepted or rejected.
panels.title: Checks by conclusion

panels.description: Percentage of completed schema checks that ended in an unexpected (non-HiveError) error. Rejected checks and expected domain errors count as successfully handled.
panels.title: Check unexpected error rate

panels.description: Checks per chart interval, stacked by conclusion. Rejected is an expected outcome (composition, breaking-change, policy, contract or input failures); unexpected error is a thrown non-HiveError. Fractional values are a smoothing artifact of rate().
panels.title: Checks over time by conclusion

panels.description: Unexpected check failures per chart interval grouped by the subsystem that raised the error. Postgres errors currently carry no source and appear as 'unknown'.
panels.title: Check unexpected errors by source

panels.description: p50/p95/p99 of the SchemaPublisher.internalCheck span, i.e. the full server-side check including composition, policy and contract evaluation (excludes GraphQL transport). No Prometheus latency metric exists for checks, so this is derived from traces. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Check duration (p50/p95/p99)

panels.description: Traces containing a SchemaPublisher.internalCheck span slower than the Schema Check Threshold variable (0ms lists every trace). The variable affects only this table. The hive.check.result attribute holds the GraphQL result type (SchemaCheckSuccess / SchemaCheckError / GitHubSchemaCheckSuccess / GitHubSchemaCheckError).
panels.title: Slow check traces (duration > $schemaCheckThreshold)

panels.description: Share of accepted and rejected checks by project type (SINGLE / FEDERATION / STITCHING) over the selected range. The model label is omitted because it is always 'modern'.
panels.title: Checks by project type

panels.description: Schema publishes completed in the selected range. Ignored means the schema was unchanged and no new version was created; rejected covers composition errors, breaking changes without --force and invalid input. Not counted here: mutex retries, distributed-cache hits within 15s, missing or invalid service names. Thrown non-HiveErrors appear only under Unexpected error.
panels.title: Publishes by conclusion

panels.description: Percentage of completed schema publishes that ended in an unexpected (non-HiveError) error. Rejected and ignored publishes count as successfully handled.
panels.title: Publish unexpected error rate

panels.description: Publishes per chart interval, stacked by conclusion. Ignored = no schema change; rejected = composition errors, breaking changes or invalid input; unexpected error = thrown non-HiveError.
panels.title: Publishes over time by conclusion

panels.description: Unexpected publish failures per chart interval grouped by the subsystem that raised the error. Postgres errors currently carry no source and appear as 'unknown'.
panels.title: Publish unexpected errors by source

panels.description: p50/p95/p99 of the SchemaPublisher.publish span, i.e. the full server-side publish including lock acquisition, composition, version creation and CDN artifact upload (excludes GraphQL transport). Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Publish duration (p50/p95/p99)

panels.description: Rate of publish outcomes by GraphQL result type, from the hive.publish.result attribute on SchemaPublisher.publish spans. SchemaPublishRetry means the registry lock for the target was held by another publish, delete or promotion; SchemaPublishMissingServiceError and SchemaPublishMissingUrlError are input problems the Prometheus counters do not record. GitHubSchemaPublishSuccess is also returned when the published schema is not composable (isValid=false). Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Publish results (trace-derived)

panels.description: Share of accepted, rejected and ignored publishes by project type over the selected range. The model label is omitted because it is always 'modern'.
panels.title: Publishes by project type

panels.description: Traces containing a SchemaPublisher.publish span slower than the Schema Publish Threshold variable (0ms lists every trace). The variable affects only this table. The hive.publish.result attribute holds the GraphQL result type.
panels.title: Slow publish traces (duration > $schemaPublishThreshold)

panels.description: Schema delete attempts in the selected range and the deletes that threw a non-HiveError. Deletes have no accepted/rejected counter: attempts are counted after auth and lock acquisition but before project-type validation, so a rejected delete on a SINGLE project is still an attempt.
panels.title: Deletes by conclusion

panels.description: Percentage of completed schema deletes that ended in an unexpected (non-HiveError) error. Domain errors such as an unsupported project type or lock contention count as successfully handled.
panels.title: Delete unexpected error rate

panels.description: Schema delete attempts per chart interval by project type, plus deletes that threw a non-HiveError. Attempts are counted before validation.
panels.title: Deletes over time

panels.description: Unexpected delete failures per chart interval grouped by the subsystem that raised the error. Postgres errors currently carry no source and appear as 'unknown'.
panels.title: Delete unexpected errors by source

panels.description: p50/p95/p99 of the SchemaPublisher.delete span, i.e. the full server-side delete including lock acquisition, composition of the remaining services and CDN artifact upload. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Delete duration (p50/p95/p99)

panels.description: Rate of delete outcomes by GraphQL result type from the hive.delete.result attribute on SchemaPublisher.delete spans. SchemaDeleteRetry means the target's registry lock was held by another operation. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Delete results (trace-derived)

panels.description: Share of delete attempts by project type over the selected range.
panels.title: Deletes by project type

panels.description: Traces containing a SchemaPublisher.delete span slower than the Schema Delete Threshold variable (0ms lists every trace). The variable affects only this table. The hive.delete.result attribute holds the GraphQL result type (SchemaDeleteSuccess / SchemaDeleteError / SchemaDeleteRetry).
panels.title: Slow delete traces (duration > $schemaDeleteThreshold)

panels.description: Schema version promotions in the selected range. There is no dedicated promotion counter: completed covers every promotion that returned a result, including domain errors such as lock contention or an invalid source; unexpected error is a thrown non-HiveError.
panels.title: Promotions by conclusion

panels.description: Percentage of completed promotions that ended in an unexpected (non-HiveError) error. Domain errors count as successfully handled.
panels.title: Promotion unexpected error rate

panels.description: Schema version promotions per chart interval. success covers every promotion that returned a result, including domain errors; failure is a thrown non-HiveError.
panels.title: Promotions over time

panels.description: Unexpected promotion failures per chart interval grouped by the subsystem that raised the error. Postgres errors currently carry no source and appear as 'unknown'.
panels.title: Promotion unexpected errors by source

panels.description: p50/p95/p99 of the SchemaPublisher.promoteSchemaVersion span, i.e. the full server-side promotion including lock acquisition, diffing against the target, contract handling and CDN artifact upload. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Promotion duration (p50/p95/p99)

panels.description: Rate of promotions by the hive.source.type attribute on SchemaPublisher.promoteSchemaVersion spans: target = promote another target's latest version, schemaVersion = promote one specific version. The span carries no result attribute, so outcome comes from the Prometheus panels above. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Promotions by source type (trace-derived)

panels.description: Traces containing a SchemaPublisher.promoteSchemaVersion span slower than the Schema Promotion Threshold variable (0ms lists every trace). The variable affects only this table. The hive.source.type attribute tells whether a target or a specific schema version was promoted.
panels.title: Slow promotion traces (duration > $schemaPromotionThreshold)

panels.description: Schema pushes in the selected range. There is no dedicated push counter: completed covers every push that returned a result, including domain errors; unexpected error is a thrown non-HiveError.
panels.title: Pushes by conclusion

panels.description: Percentage of completed pushes that ended in an unexpected (non-HiveError) error. Domain errors count as successfully handled.
panels.title: Push unexpected error rate

panels.description: Schema pushes per chart interval. success covers every push that returned a result, including domain errors; failure is a thrown non-HiveError.
panels.title: Pushes over time

panels.description: Unexpected push failures per chart interval grouped by the subsystem that raised the error. Postgres errors currently carry no source and appear as 'unknown'.
panels.title: Push unexpected errors by source

panels.description: p50/p95/p99 of the SchemaPusher.push span, i.e. the full server-side push. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Push duration (p50/p95/p99)

panels.description: Rate of push outcomes from the hive.push.result attribute on SchemaPusher.push spans: success when the push was accepted, error when it returned a domain error. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Push results (trace-derived)

panels.description: Traces containing a SchemaPusher.push span slower than the Schema Push Threshold variable (0ms lists every trace). The variable affects only this table. The hive.push.result attribute is success or error.
panels.title: Slow push traces (duration > $schemaPushThreshold)

panels.description: Composition results from schema-service per chart interval. success means the composition ran to completion and includes results that contain composition errors (those surface as rejected checks and publishes); failure means the worker threw (crash, no idle worker); timeout is the 60s composition timeout; cache=hit means the result was replayed from the distributed cache. OOM debug dumps counts compositions that exceeded the worker memory limit, measured by the subgraph debug upload the API writes for each one. A single check or publish may call the service one to three times.
panels.title: Composition outcomes (schema-service)

panels.description: Rate of composition calls whose result contained at least one composition or validation error, by project type, from the hive.composition.error.count attribute on CompositionOrchestrator.composeAndValidate spans. This is the closest available signal for composition failures as a cause of rejected checks and publishes; schema-service timeouts also appear here (error.count=1). Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Compositions returning errors (trace-derived)

panels.description: p95 of time a composition waits in the schema-service queue, runs in a worker thread, and the total of both. Only cache misses are measured; queue wait is observed for every dequeued request, worker and total only when the worker returns (failures and timeouts are excluded). Buckets are coarse (50ms to 45s), so values are interpolated.
panels.title: Composition duration p95 (queue / worker / total)

panels.description: Largest heap growth caused by a single composition per interval, as a percentage of the worker's max old-generation size (hive.composition.heap.percent on the schema-service request span; the worker reports heap after minus heap before the composition). It measures how much of the memory budget one composition consumes, not total worker usage. Values approaching 100 precede out-of-memory compositions. Uses max_over_time because quantiles on span attributes are unsupported by the local Tempo setup.
panels.title: Composition heap growth (max % of worker limit)

panels.description: policy-service checkPolicy calls per chart interval, made by schema checks and publishes whose project or organization has a schema policy configured. Summed across all targets because the target label is a per-target UUID.
panels.title: Policy checks (policy-service)

panels.description: p50/p95 duration of policy-service checkPolicy, aggregated across targets and converted from seconds to milliseconds. Only successful checks are observed; a check that throws never stops the timer.
panels.title: Policy check duration (p50/p95)

panels.description: p95 of the ClickHouse queries that conditional breaking-change detection runs during checks, publishes, deletes and promotions (total request counts, per-coordinate counts, top operations and clients for affected coordinates), converted to milliseconds. Only successful queries are observed. count_fields_v2_* is also used by the UI. For publish, delete and promotion these queries run while the registry lock is held.
panels.title: Conditional breaking-change usage lookups p95 (ClickHouse)

panels.description: Versioned and latest artifact uploads (SDL, services, metadata, supergraph, contracts) made by publish, delete and promotion, per chart interval, by destination bucket and HTTP status. One series per primary and mirror bucket, so divergence between them is visible here. Non-2xx responses surface as unexpected errors with source 's3 <origin>'.
panels.title: CDN artifact writes by destination and status

panels.description: Workflow jobs that registry operations enqueue: schemaChangeNotification delivers webhook alerts after a publish or delete, schemaProposalComposition composes a proposal after a check. errored counts failed attempts (each attempt is retried); the failed_total metric never fires for webhooks because exhausted retries are reported as success. Slack, Teams and Discord notifications are sent inline from the API and have no metric.
panels.title: Registry background jobs (workflows)

panels.description: Time publish, delete and promotion wait to acquire the per-target registry lock (Mutex.lock span, lock.id = registry-lock:<targetId>). This is wait time, not hold time. Sustained waits mean concurrent operations on the same target; contention also shows as SchemaPublishRetry / SchemaDeleteRetry in the publish and delete rows. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Registry lock wait (p50/p95)

panels.description: Rate of registry-lock acquisitions that gave up (MutexResourceLockedError after the retry budget). These surface to the caller as SchemaPublishRetry / SchemaDeleteRetry or a promotion 'Please try again later' error, and are not unexpected errors. Trace sampling applies.
panels.title: Registry lock contention

list.description: Only filters the "Slow check traces" table in the Schema Check row; charts and stats are unaffected. The default 0ms lists every trace; pick or type a value such as 500ms to keep only slower ones.
list.label: Schema Check Threshold
list.name: schemaCheckThreshold

list.description: Only filters the "Slow publish traces" table in the Schema Publish row; charts and stats are unaffected. The default 0ms lists every trace; pick or type a value such as 500ms to keep only slower ones.
list.label: Schema Publish Threshold
list.name: schemaPublishThreshold

list.description: Only filters the "Slow delete traces" table in the Schema Delete row; charts and stats are unaffected. The default 0ms lists every trace; pick or type a value such as 500ms to keep only slower ones.
list.label: Schema Delete Threshold
list.name: schemaDeleteThreshold

list.description: Only filters the "Slow promotion traces" table in the Schema Promotion row; charts and stats are unaffected. The default 0ms lists every trace; pick or type a value such as 500ms to keep only slower ones.
list.label: Schema Promotion Threshold
list.name: schemaPromotionThreshold

list.description: Only filters the "Slow push traces" table in the Schema Push row; charts and stats are unaffected. The default 0ms lists every trace; pick or type a value such as 500ms to keep only slower ones.
list.label: Schema Push Threshold
list.name: schemaPushThreshold
